CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zuexact computes sums of doubles exactly and rounds once, so results are the correctly rounded true value on every platform and in every element order. It vendors Radford Neal’s xsum (MIT) and exposes it as R functions with the xsum_ prefix (xsum() itself is the main entry point) and as a registered C table for other packages. Zero hard runtime dependencies. It never does arbitrary precision, decimals, or compensated-but-inexact summation (Kahan and friends live in PreciseSums).

.agents/design.md is the specification and .agents/roadmap.md the plan to 0.1.0. They outrank this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-13: Stages 0 to 3. Exported: xsum(), xsum_mean(), xsum_weighted_mean(), xsum_cumsum(), xsum_dot(), xsum_sqnorm(), xsum_norm(), zuexact_info(). xsum is vendored, patched, and checked by upstream’s own checker and fuzzer. Accumulator values, matrices, grouped sums and the C table are not built yet (Stages 4 to 6).

Stage tracking

Progress toward 0.1.0 is tracked as GitHub sub-issues of v0.1.0 (#2); submission is #12.

  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it and linking to that section. Every tracking issue carries the stage label.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request with Closes #<n> in the body. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Merges are merge commits. The repository ruleset on main requires pull requests and allows only the merge method; squash is refused.

Versioning

Develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading in the last roadmap stage. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it. Until then the R API and the C table may change freely; no sibling depends on zuexact yet (daffiz and qio are the candidate consumers of the C table).

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
air format .                                     # format R sources
tools/vendor/verify                              # vendored tree == upstream + patches
tools/xsum-check/run [iters [seed]]              # upstream checker and fuzzer
tools/run-benchmarks                             # small/large threshold (C, no R)

The first five are the development loop; the tools/ scripts are for vendoring changes and need curl and a C compiler.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • One pass, then a rescan only when the result is not finite (src/zxe_sum.c). The rescan must skip exactly what na.rm = TRUE removed, including a complex element dropped because its other part is NaN; it once did not, and xsum(c(NA, Inf), na.rm = TRUE) gave NA.

  • ALTREP() decides how a vector is read. ALTREP vectors go through *_GET_REGION into a stack block; REAL_RO() on one would materialise it.

  • One rounding. Every function rounds the exact value once, except where its documentation states the count (xsum_norm() two, xsum_weighted_mean() three). Never add an intermediate double between accumulation and the final round.

  • zuexact.so exports R_init_zuexact only ($(C_VISIBILITY) in src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win), and links no stdio, abort, exit or RNG symbol. tests/testthat/test-abi.R audits both on Linux and macOS.

  • TwoProduct must not be contracted (design §9, §13). The file that splits products with fma() carries #pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF and keeps p = x*y and e = fma(x, y, -p) in separate statements.

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient and self-contained. Each test_that() builds its own inputs; global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text: expect_error(..., class = "zuexact_invalid_argument").
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of done.
  • Oracles before hand-written cases (design §11): exact rationals with gmp, PreciseSums::fsum(), the Math.sumPrecise test262 vectors, and the Ogita–Rump–Oishi ill-conditioned generators.
  • Helpers live in tests/testthat/helper-*.R: helper-abi.R reads the shared object’s exported and undefined symbols with nm; helper-vendor.R defines selftest(), which sums through both xsum accumulators directly; helper-oracle.R holds the exact rational oracle (exact_sum(), exact_dot()), whose round_bigq() exists because gmp’s as.double() truncates instead of rounding.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes, apart from “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. CI green on every leg, including nold (R without long doubles), which is the leg this package exists for. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

CI through pedrobtz/r-actions is the pre-submission check; no win-builder, macOS builder or R-hub. cran-comments.md lists the CI legs. The pretest does not read explanations, so fix every NOTE. After acceptance: tag 0.1.0 on the commit in CRAN-SUBMISSION, publish the GitHub release, bump to 0.1.0.9000, close #2 and #12.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Keep prose simple and short, in en-GB.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case. Internal C symbols are prefixed zxe_; the public C table and header use zuexact_.
  • Zero hard runtime dependencies.

Continuous integration

Workflows call pedrobtz/r-actions: R-CMD-check.yaml (r-cmd-check.yml@v1, quick on pull requests, full on main, nold: true), coverage.yaml (coverage.yml, pinned to a commit because it holds a write token; badge on gh-pages because main takes no direct pushes), native-checks.yaml (sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers, CRAN special checks), vendor.yaml, vendor-upstream.yaml (weekly), and xsum-check.yaml (upstream’s checker, fuzzer and the threshold benchmark on three OSes, outside R). pkgdown.yaml deploys with force: false so it does not overwrite the badge commit. The full-ci label runs the full profile on a pull request.

Vendored native code

xsum by Radford M. Neal, MIT, pinned at tag stable-version-3, commit b766b3e (2024-11-13), in src/vendor/xsum/. tools/vendor/manifest.tsv pins it; tools/vendor/checksums.sha256 records the installed files; the one local patch is tools/patches/xsum/0001-no-stdio-exact-only.patch. Never edit src/vendor/ by hand: change the patch and run tools/vendor/fetch. The vendor.yaml workflow rejects a pull request that changes the tree without the manifest and checksums, and vendor-upstream.yaml opens an issue weekly when upstream tags a newer stable version. CRAN’s compiled-code check applies to vendored code: no printf, abort, exit or system RNG may be linked, even behind a debug switch. Remove them with a patch, never with a justification.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects. Never push to main; work on a branch and open a pull request. One pull request per roadmap stage, titled as the stage, closing its sub-issue.
